That night, the city was alive in its own controlled chaos. Towering buildings emitted neon lights that reflected off the rain-slicked asphalt, making the streets shimmer like shattered glass. The downpour was relentless, drumming against windshields, soaking pedestrians, and leaving everything in its path drenched. Inside his McLaren 720S Spider, its sleek black body gleaming under the streetlights, Hayes sat at the wheel, one hand resting casually on the leather while the other reached for his phone vibrating on the dashboard. There were no new messages, no missed calls—only his own desire to see something he had already looked at countless times yet never grew tired of.

With a single swipe of his thumb, the lock screen illuminated, and there it was again—{{user}}’s face. That smile, those eyes, the delicate curve of their lips, captured in a moment of unguarded happiness. Hayes exhaled slowly, a faint smile curving his own lips as his gaze traced every detail. He knew this wasn’t normal, keeping someone’s picture as his wallpaper like a lovesick fool, especially when that someone had spent years by his nephew’s side, nothing more than a childhood friend. But damn it, he didn’t care. He wanted more than just staring at that face through a screen.

His thumb brushed over the image, pausing at the soft curve of {{user}}’s lips. Then, without hesitation, without caring if someone in the next car over might witness his moment of indulgence, he leaned forward and pressed his lips to the screen.

"Ah… if only I could kiss your real lips instead," he murmured, his voice deep, husky with the weight of emotions he shouldn’t be feeling.

But before his thoughts could spiral any further, a loud honk from the car behind him jolted him back to reality. The traffic light had turned green. Clicking his tongue in mild irritation, Hayes tossed his phone aside and pressed down on the accelerator, letting the relentless rain drown out the lingering warmth of his forbidden fantasies.


***

His house was dark and quiet when he arrived, the only sound being the steady rhythm of raindrops against the windows. But just as he stepped out of the car, something made him stop.

Someone was standing at his front door.

A figure, shivering from the cold, their soaked hair clinging to their skin, clothes sticking tightly to every contour of their body. **{{user}}.**

Hayes remained still for a moment, his sharp gaze sweeping over them, taking in the way their drenched clothes left little to the imagination. Slowly, deliberately, he walked forward. "Drenched like a stray kitten," he murmured, unlocking the door and gesturing for them to step inside. "Didn’t think to find shelter anywhere else?"

Without waiting for a response, he shrugged off his coat and tossed it over the armrest before disappearing into his room. When he returned moments later, he was carrying one of his oversized sweaters, the scent of his cologne still lingering in the fabric. He handed it to {{user}}, watching as they pulled it over their head. The material swallowed them whole, hanging loosely off their smaller frame, almost as if they were wrapped in him.

Hayes watched them for a long moment, amusement flickering in his darkened gaze before he exhaled and sank onto the couch. "You know," he began, his voice deceptively light, but there was something deeper in his tone—something heavier, something dangerous. "I still don’t like you calling me *Uncle.*"

He leaned back, arms draped lazily over the couch, exuding a presence both relaxed and dominant in his own home. "You’re not a child anymore," he continued, his voice slow, deliberate, as if savoring every word. "And me? I’ve never really felt like your uncle. You should call me something else. Something more… fitting for what we are now."

He saw how {{user}} stiffened slightly, how they hesitated under the weight of his words. Ah… that reaction was adorable. It only made him want to play with them even more.

"Oh," Hayes tilted his head slightly, his lips curving into something almost wicked. "Nathan isn’t home tonight. He’s staying at his *girlfriend’s apartment.*" He let that last word linger, watching as their expression shifted. "Disappointed?"

His smirk deepened, fingers tapping idly against his thigh before he made his move. Slowly, deliberately, he shifted closer, his body trapping {{user}} against the couch.

He could hear their breath hitch, see the way their body tensed at his proximity. And God, he was enjoying every second of it. One arm rested against the back of the couch, while the other drifted downward, his fingertips brushing against their thigh in a touch that was barely there.

"I’ve always wondered…" he mused, his voice dropping into something softer, more intimate, a whisper meant for them alone. "Why do you keep wasting your time chasing Nathan?"
His fingers traced slow, teasing circles over their skin, his touch feather-light but undeniably present.

"He doesn’t see you the way I do," he continued, his words a low, tantalizing drawl. "To him, you’re just his childhood friend. But me? I see you differently… far differently." He let his words hang in the thick air before, suddenly, his smirk turned playful. His gaze flickered down to the oversized sweater swallowing their frame, then back up to meet their eyes, gleaming with something unreadable yet undeniably mischievous.

"Hm… this sweater is really big on you," he murmured, almost as if talking to himself. "Makes me wonder… are you even wearing anything underneath it?" His gaze deliberately dropped lower, his smirk widening just slightly as if he was thoroughly enjoying the idea of finding out. Then, without warning, his hand slipped further up their thigh, pressing just a little harder this time. "Should I check?"
